title: Residue field of a point of a fibre product
statement: Let $f:X\to S$ and $g:Y\to S$ be morphisms of schemes [def-pc-scheme] with fibre product $X\times_SY$ and projections $p,q$ [def-pc-fibre-product]. Let $z\in X\times_SY$, put $x=p(z)$, $y=q(z)$, $s=f(x)=g(y)$, and let $\mathfrak p$ be the kernel of the ring map $\kappa(x)\otimes_{\kappa(s)}\kappa(y)\to\kappa(z)$, $a\otimes b\mapsto p^\sharp(a)q^\sharp(b)$, where $p^\sharp:\kappa(x)\to\kappa(z)$, $q^\sharp:\kappa(y)\to\kappa(z)$ are the maps induced by $p$ and $q$ on residue fields [def-weil-residue-field] (this $\mathfrak p$ is the prime ideal attached to $z$ in [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-points]). Then the induced field homomorphism from the residue field $\kappa(\mathfrak p)$ of $\mathfrak p$ (the fraction field of $(\kappa(x)\otimes_{\kappa(s)}\kappa(y))/\mathfrak p$) to $\kappa(z)$ is an isomorphism; it is compatible with the maps from $\kappa(x)$ and from $\kappa(y)$. In particular, if $(\kappa(x)\otimes_{\kappa(s)}\kappa(y))/\mathfrak p$ is a field, then $(\kappa(x)\otimes_{\kappa(s)}\kappa(y))/\mathfrak p\to\kappa(z)$ is an isomorphism of extensions of $\kappa(x)$ and of $\kappa(y)$.

source.place: Schemes, Lemma 01JT (schemes-lemma-points-fibre-product, line 3265), last sentence of the statement: 'The residue field of z corresponds to the residue field of the prime p'; the existing node lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-points states the rest of 01JT without this sentence

proof.text: Notation: $R=\kappa(x)\otimes_{\kappa(s)}\kappa(y)$ with $\iota_x:\kappa(x)\to R$, $a\mapsto a\otimes1$, and $\iota_y:\kappa(y)\to R$, $b\mapsto1\otimes b$; $f^\sharp:\kappa(s)\to\kappa(x)$, $g^\sharp:\kappa(s)\to\kappa(y)$, $p^\sharp:\kappa(x)\to\kappa(z)$, $q^\sharp:\kappa(y)\to\kappa(z)$ the maps induced on residue fields [def-weil-residue-field]; for a point $w$ of a scheme $W$, $j_w:\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(w)\to W$ is the canonical morphism and $\xi$ denotes the unique point of the spectrum of a field [def-weil-affine-spectrum]. *Step 1: the map $\psi$ and the prime $\mathfrak p$.* By [lem-weil-pbc-residue-field-point-naturality] applied to $f$ at $x$ and to $p$ at $z$ (note $p(z)=x$): $f\circ j_x=j_s\circ\operatorname{Spec}(f^\sharp)$ and $p\circ j_z=j_x\circ\operatorname{Spec}(p^\sharp)$, so $f\circ p\circ j_z=j_s\circ\operatorname{Spec}(f^\sharp)\circ\operatorname{Spec}(p^\sharp)=j_s\circ\operatorname{Spec}(p^\sharp\circ f^\sharp)$ (contravariant functoriality of $\operatorname{Spec}$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum]); likewise $g\circ q\circ j_z=j_s\circ\operatorname{Spec}(q^\sharp\circ g^\sharp)$. Since $f\circ p=g\circ q$ [def-pc-fibre-product], the morphisms $j_s\circ\operatorname{Spec}(p^\sharp\circ f^\sharp)$ and $j_s\circ\operatorname{Spec}(q^\sharp\circ g^\sharp)$ from $\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(z)$ to $S$ are equal, and by the injectivity of $(s,\varphi)\mapsto j_s\circ\operatorname{Spec}(\varphi)$ in [lem-weil-pbc-morphism-from-spec-field] $p^\sharp\circ f^\sharp=q^\sharp\circ g^\sharp$. Hence $p^\sharp$ and $q^\sharp$ are $\kappa(s)$-algebra maps for the same $\kappa(s)$-algebra structure on $\kappa(z)$, and the universal property of the tensor product of $\kappa(s)$-algebras gives the ring map $\psi:R\to\kappa(z)$, $a\otimes b\mapsto p^\sharp(a)q^\sharp(b)$, with $\psi\circ\iota_x=p^\sharp$, $\psi\circ\iota_y=q^\sharp$. Its kernel $\mathfrak p$ is prime, since $R/\mathfrak p$ embeds in the field $\kappa(z)$. (This is the construction of the Stacks proof: $z$ as a morphism $\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(z)\to X\times_SY$, Lemma 01J9.)

source.place: Schemes, Lemma 01JT (schemes-lemma-points-fibre-product, line 3265), proof, first paragraph (lines 3282-3298), using Lemma 01J9 (schemes-lemma-characterize-points)

proof.text: *Step 2: the morphism $T:\operatorname{Spec}R\to X\times_SY$.* In $R$ one has $\iota_x\circ f^\sharp=\iota_y\circ g^\sharp$ ($c\otimes1=1\otimes c$ for $c\in\kappa(s)$). With step 1's identities $f\circ j_x=j_s\circ\operatorname{Spec}(f^\sharp)$ and $g\circ j_y=j_s\circ\operatorname{Spec}(g^\sharp)$ [lem-weil-pbc-residue-field-point-naturality] this gives $f\circ j_x\circ\operatorname{Spec}(\iota_x)=j_s\circ\operatorname{Spec}(\iota_x\circ f^\sharp)=j_s\circ\operatorname{Spec}(\iota_y\circ g^\sharp)=g\circ j_y\circ\operatorname{Spec}(\iota_y)$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum]. By the universal property of the fibre product [def-pc-fibre-product] there is a unique morphism $T:\operatorname{Spec}R\to X\times_SY$ with $p\circ T=j_x\circ\operatorname{Spec}(\iota_x)$ and $q\circ T=j_y\circ\operatorname{Spec}(\iota_y)$. (This is the dotted arrow of the Stacks proof, before passing to $R/\mathfrak p$.)

proof.text: *Step 3: $T\circ\operatorname{Spec}(\psi)=j_z$.* Both are morphisms $\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(z)\to X\times_SY$. By step 2 and step 1, $p\circ T\circ\operatorname{Spec}(\psi)=j_x\circ\operatorname{Spec}(\iota_x)\circ\operatorname{Spec}(\psi)=j_x\circ\operatorname{Spec}(\psi\circ\iota_x)=j_x\circ\operatorname{Spec}(p^\sharp)=p\circ j_z$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum], [lem-weil-pbc-residue-field-point-naturality]; in the same way $q\circ T\circ\operatorname{Spec}(\psi)=j_y\circ\operatorname{Spec}(q^\sharp)=q\circ j_z$. By the uniqueness in the universal property of the fibre product [def-pc-fibre-product], $T\circ\operatorname{Spec}(\psi)=j_z$.

source.place: Schemes, Lemma 01JT (schemes-lemma-points-fibre-product), proof, second paragraph (the diagram with the dotted arrow, lines 3300-3326, Section 01J5 schemes-section-points); the residue-field verification is omitted there and written out here

proof.text: *Step 4: the map $\lambda:\kappa(\mathfrak p)\to\kappa(z)$ and $T(\mathfrak p)=z$.* Apply [lem-weil-pbc-spec-field-point-residue-field] (3) to $\psi:R\to K=\kappa(z)$: $\operatorname{Spec}(\psi)$ maps $\xi$ to $\ker\psi=\mathfrak p$, and the field map $\lambda:\kappa(\mathfrak p)\to\kappa(z)$ induced by $\operatorname{Spec}(\psi)$ on residue fields is the unique ring map from $\kappa(\mathfrak p)=\operatorname{Frac}(R/\mathfrak p)$ (clause (1) of the same node) extending the injection $R/\mathfrak p\to\kappa(z)$ induced by $\psi$; so $\lambda$ is the induced field homomorphism of the statement, and $\lambda\circ\pi=\psi$ for $\pi:R\to\kappa(\mathfrak p)$. By [lem-weil-pbc-morphism-from-spec-field] applied to $\operatorname{Spec}(\psi):\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(z)\to\operatorname{Spec}R$, $\operatorname{Spec}(\psi)=j_{\mathfrak p}\circ\operatorname{Spec}(\lambda)$. By the same node $j_z(\xi)=z$, so by step 3 $T(\mathfrak p)=T(\operatorname{Spec}(\psi)(\xi))=j_z(\xi)=z$.

source.place: Schemes, Lemma 01JT (schemes-lemma-points-fibre-product), proof, second paragraph (the diagram with the dotted arrow, lines 3300-3326, Section 01J5 schemes-section-points); the residue-field verification is omitted there and written out here

proof.text: *Step 5: $\lambda\circ T^\sharp=\mathrm{id}_{\kappa(z)}$.* Let $T^\sharp:\kappa(z)=\kappa(T(\mathfrak p))\to\kappa(\mathfrak p)$ be the map induced by $T$ on residue fields at $\mathfrak p$ (step 4) [def-weil-residue-field]. By [lem-weil-pbc-residue-field-point-naturality] applied to $T$ at $\mathfrak p$, $T\circ j_{\mathfrak p}=j_z\circ\operatorname{Spec}(T^\sharp)$. With steps 3 and 4: $j_z=T\circ\operatorname{Spec}(\psi)=T\circ j_{\mathfrak p}\circ\operatorname{Spec}(\lambda)=j_z\circ\operatorname{Spec}(T^\sharp)\circ\operatorname{Spec}(\lambda)=j_z\circ\operatorname{Spec}(\lambda\circ T^\sharp)$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum]. Also $j_z=j_z\circ\operatorname{Spec}(\mathrm{id}_{\kappa(z)})$. By the injectivity of $(z,\varphi)\mapsto j_z\circ\operatorname{Spec}(\varphi)$ in [lem-weil-pbc-morphism-from-spec-field], $\lambda\circ T^\sharp=\mathrm{id}_{\kappa(z)}$.

proof.text: *Step 6: conclusion.* $\lambda$ is a ring map between fields, hence injective (its kernel is a proper ideal of the field $\kappa(\mathfrak p)$), and it is surjective by step 5; so $\lambda$ is an isomorphism, with inverse $T^\sharp$. The maps from $\kappa(x)$ and $\kappa(y)$ to $\kappa(\mathfrak p)$ are $\pi\circ\iota_x$ and $\pi\circ\iota_y$, and $\lambda\circ\pi\circ\iota_x=\psi\circ\iota_x=p^\sharp$, $\lambda\circ\pi\circ\iota_y=q^\sharp$ (steps 1 and 4): $\lambda$ is compatible with the maps from $\kappa(x)$ and $\kappa(y)$. If $R/\mathfrak p$ is a field, the inclusion $R/\mathfrak p\to\operatorname{Frac}(R/\mathfrak p)=\kappa(\mathfrak p)$ is an isomorphism, and $R/\mathfrak p\to\kappa(z)$, the composite of it with $\lambda$, is an isomorphism of extensions of $\kappa(x)$ and of $\kappa(y)$.

lean.statement: theorem exists_residueField_equiv_ofPointTensor {X Y S : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ S) (g : Y ⟶ S) (z : ↑(pullback f g)) : let T := Triplet.ofPoint z let ψ := (ofPointTensor z).hom let p := RingHom.ker ψ letI : p.IsPrime := RingHom.ker_isPrime ψ (∃ e : p.ResidueField ≃+* (pullback f g).residueField z, e.toRingHom.comp (algebraMap T.tensor p.ResidueField) = ψ ∧ e.toRingHom.comp ((algebraMap T.tensor p.ResidueField).comp T.tensorInl.hom) = ((pullback.fst f g).residueFieldMap z).hom ∧ e.toRingHom.comp ((algebraMap T.tensor p.ResidueField).comp T.tensorInr.hom) = ((pullback.snd f g).residueFieldMap z).hom) ∧ (IsField (T.tensor ⧸ p) → ∃ e : (T.tensor ⧸ p) ≃+* (pullback f g).residueField z, e.toRingHom.comp (Ideal.Quotient.mk p) = ψ ∧ e.toRingHom.comp ((Ideal.Quotient.mk p).comp T.tensorInl.hom) = ((pullback.fst f g).residueFieldMap z).hom ∧ e.toRingHom.comp ((Ideal.Quotient.mk p).comp T.tensorInr.hom) = ((pullback.snd f g).residueFieldMap z).hom)
